An EHDS-compliant demonstration platform: An EHDS-compliant demonstration platform built with Eclipse EDC-V, DCore, CFM, Neo4j, FHIR R4, and OMOP CDM. The project implements the European Health Data Space regulation through a 5-layer knowledge graph architecture, from DSP Marketplace discovery to Ontology alignment, enabling sovereign health data exchange between data holders and approved research users. Explore the architecture →
Security and data protection are tested: Security and data protection are tested by the project itself with tools anyone can run on the repository, and every finding is either fixed or named as open. The test of 2026-10-15 found ten findings, F1 to F10: after the fixes nine are closed and one is reviewed and accepted (F3, the published development default key of the local compose stack; Azure takes its keys from Vault). None of this is an independent penetration test or a certification. How the platform is operated for real, role by role, is the operational guideline in the Operations section.

Klarbefund is the iPhone app of this pro: Klarbefund is the iPhone app of this project. It scans a paper lab report, reads the values on the device, codes them with LOINC, keeps them encrypted on the phone and exports them as FHIR and OMOP, or sends them to the person's own record on the hub when they say so. Every screenshot shows invented data from the app's own demo dataset.

The European Health Data Space is Regula: The European Health Data Space is Regulation (EU) 2025/327. This section says what the integration hub implements of it, article by article: the page, the route or the file that does it, the test that shows it, and where it falls short, with the issue that tracks the gap. Article numbers are the adopted ones; older material in the repository may still cite the 2022 proposal, and the numbering page maps one to the other.

Regulation (EU) 2025/327 applies in stag: Regulation (EU) 2025/327 applies in stages (Art. 105): generally from 26 March 2027, secondary use in full from 26 March 2029, further data categories from 26 March 2031. The 2026 implementing acts turn articles into specifications: dataset descriptions (2026/2098), health data in the EUDI Wallet with assurance levels (2026/2099), MyHealth@EU (2026/2083).

Simpl-Open is the Commission's open-sour: Simpl-Open is the Commission's open-source middleware for European data spaces; the EHDS secondary-use data space is in its first wave. The hub meets it as a connector outside its agent, over DSP and DCP, and keeps the health rules in its own extension (ADR-064).

eIDAS 2.0 obliges every Member State to: eIDAS 2.0 obliges every Member State to offer a wallet; 2026/2099 makes it how persons identify for the EHDS, at assurance level substantial from 2027 and high from 2030. The German wallet d-you goes into production on 2 January 2027. The European Business Wallet, still in negotiation, lets a person act for an organisation, as a researcher applying for a permit does.

The Dataspace Protocol came from IDSA an: The Dataspace Protocol came from IDSA and is standardised by the Eclipse Dataspace Working Group. DSP negotiates contracts and transfers, DCP proves identity with verifiable credentials, Data Plane Signaling lets the control plane start and stop a data plane. Simpl-Open runs Eclipse EDC too, so these are where the two meet.
